title: Trace backfill and dashboard grooming - Oct 8 2026
content:
Purpose
Runbook-style notes for the week: coordinate the trace backfill, groom the cost dashboards, and land quick telemetry wins to reduce ingestion spend. This is a working capture — mostly action items, short logs from standups, and decisions we made in the Wednesday sync.

Summary at-a-glance
- Backfill window: target 2026-09-20 -> 2026-10-05 full ingest for prod-traces (partial already present).
- Sampling changes: roll to route-level adaptive sampling (p50/p95 focused) on 2026-10-10 canary.
- Dashboard refresh: retired old "Trace Volume (raw)" chart, replaced with derived "Trace Cost per Route" (est cost tokenization).
- Immediate cost wins identified: drop noisy internal debug spans (svc-debug-*), compress span tags for high-volume RPCs, and tune agent batching to 200ms.

Weekly standup logs (mon -> fri)
Mon 2026-10-05
- Quick sync with infra: backfill plan validated; we have an extra 1.2TB cluster window on 10/9 for accelerated ingest. (Daniel)
- Observed: sudden spike in span counts for /chat/generate between 2026-09-29 00:00 and 09-29 06:00 UTC; root cause probable load-test that wasn't tagged. File: ENGOBS-4123.
- TODO: script to dedupe duplicate traces from earlier failed job (Priya).

Tue 2026-10-06
- Dashboard grooming session: agreed on metrics, wireframes for "Trace Cost per Route" and "Trace Size distribution by model". Liam prototyped a heatmap.
- Note: currently we over-index on top-level tags causing cardinality explosion; immediate fix: add truncation step in ingest lambda. (Sreya + Telemetry infra)
- Decision: sampling adjustments will be route-aware rather than service-aware to preserve tail signals for prioritized routes.

Wed 2026-10-07 — lunchtime sync (major decisions)
- Canaries: 10% adaptive sampling on non-priority routes, 100% for payment/hosting routes. Target rollout 10/10.
- Backfill strategy: phased backfill by model family (gptx-llm -> llama-family -> search-reranker) to avoid KV cache blowouts. Backfill script PR: #289 in telemetry repo.
- Cost estimate: ingest cost projected to increase by $1.1k/day during backfill window. Plan to offset using the 1.2TB cluster and a temporary quota bump. Finance notified (ticket ENGOBS-4187).
- Action: Daniel to open infra change for temp quota; Priya to run dedupe and validate checksums; Ava to update Confluence backfill plan.

Thu 2026-10-08 (today) — grooming + exec huddle prep
- Groomed dashboard tree and moved low-value charts to an "archived" section.
- Added a derived metric: "span-cost-estimate" = span_count * avg_bytes * unit_ingest_cost — used to drive per-route alerts.
- Observability alert change: create a weekly rollup alert for "projected ingest cost > $5k/week" to avoid surprises. (blocked: need billing API token rotation)
- Quick note to self: sample log lines still include full user prompts in debug spans -> privacy risk. Immediate stop-gap: redact span.metadata.prompt until we can roll out hashing (Priya).

Fri 2026-10-09 (next steps)
- Scheduled: canary rollout for adaptive sampling (10% traffic) 10/10 02:00 UTC. Rollback plan documented.
- QA checklist for canary: verify p95 latency drift < 5%, compare span retention for payment routes, confirm no missing traces for KV cache warmups. (Liam)
- Backfill staged: first chunk (gptx-llm) queued for 10/09 22:00 UTC. Monitor ingest QPS and S3 throughput.

Action items (owner — ETA)
- Priya Natarajan — dedupe script + privacy redaction patch (PR: telemetry #289) — ETA 2026-10-09.
- Daniel Singh — infra quota bump + temp cluster reservation for 10/09 -> 10/12 — ETA 2026-10-08 (done), verify billing alarm.
- Liam O'Connor — dashboard heatmap polish + alert integration (Grafana panels + Loki queries) — ETA 2026-10-11.
- Ava Martinez — update Confluence playbook, add rollback steps, link to ENGOBS tickets — ETA 2026-10-09.
- Sreya Rao — add truncation step in ingest pipeline and run canary for tag compression — ETA 2026-10-10.

Open questions / risks
- Risk: backfill may push KV cache eviction that causes latency spikes for live traffic. Mitigation: stagger backfill and monitor cache hit-rate; fallback route to older model instance pool if hit-rate drops > 10%.
- Question: should we keep full-span retention for developer sandbox orgs? Sandbox traffic causes 14% of spans but low business value. Proposal: default to 7-day retention for sandboxes (ask legal about retention policy).
- Unknown: actual unit cost for compressed spans vs raw — need benchmarking from Storage team for compressed write throughput.

Notes to reviewers (informal)
- This doc is intentionally rough. If you want to split into two smaller docs (backfill plan vs dashboard grooming) say so and I will extract.
- If you see missing Slack threads or ticket refs, add them to linked_artifacts.

Quick metrics snapshot (today)
- Global span ingestion: 1.8M spans/day (baseline pre-backfill: 1.2M).
- Top 3 noisy routes by span count: /chat/generate, /embeddings/batch, /model/eval.
- Current average span size: 640 bytes. Estimated cost per 100k spans: $2.8 (ingest only).

Reference commands / useful snippets
- Backfill dry-run: python scripts/backfill_traces.py --start 2026-09-20 --end 2026-09-30 --dry-run
- Dedupe check: s3cmd ls s3://prod-traces/ | grep duplicate-prefix | xargs -n1 sha256sum
- Dashboard rebuild: scripts/grafana_sync.py --sync dashboards/trace-cost.json

Decision log (short)
- 2026-10-07: Route-aware adaptive sampling accepted (reason: preserves tail for critical routes with less cost than 100% retention).
- 2026-10-08: Archive low-value charts and add "cost per route" derived metric (reason: focus on dollar impact).

If you read nothing else: monitor canary on 10/10 and be ready to pause backfill if p95 latency increases > 7% for any route.

-- end of notes --
